macros.name: DefaultOptionsFile
macros.doc: Instead of giving optional parameters to the \lettrine command, it is possible to set them on a per character basis in a second config file (suggested by Pascal Kockaert): \renewcommand{\DefaultOptionsFile}{<filename>} in the preamble will force this file to be read ‘AtBeginDocument’.

macros.name: lettrine
macros.doc: Adding \usepackage{lettrine} in the preamble of a document defines the command \lettrine, the simplest use of which is \lettrine{<letter>}{<text>}. It produces a dropped capital <letter> (2 lines high), followed by <text> typeset in small caps, and the rest of the paragraph is wrapped around the dropped capital.

macros.name: LettrineFontHook
macros.doc: \LettrineFontHook can also be used to change the colour of all initials in a (part of) document: \renewcommand{\LettrineFontHook}{\color[gray]{0.5}} will colour the initials following this command in grey.

macros.name: LettrineHeight
macros.doc: Three dimensions, \LettrineHeight, \LettrineDepth and \LettrineWidth hold the final size of the initial (height and depth being measured from the paragraph’s n-th baseline if lines=n.
